Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, 
after the draft finalized by the Lead, Zinc, Cadmium, Tin, Antimony and Their Alloys Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. 

This standard was first published in 1967 with a view to encourage conservation of tin through 
the use of refined secondary tin for alloy additions for manufacture of bronzes, antifriction alloys, 
soft solders etc. Tin covered in this standard is also recommended for tinning by hot-dip or 
electrolytic process. This standard was subsequently revised in 1979. In this revision the follow- 
ing modifications have been made: 

a) A new clause on references has been incorporated; and 

b) Clauses on chemical analysis and marking have been modified. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 *Rules for rounding off' numerical values ( revised y. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard. 



IS 4280 : 1992 



Indian Standard 



REFINED SECONDARY TIN — INGOT — 

SPECIFICATION 

( Second Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the requirements for 
refined secondary tin in the form of ingots. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standaads are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard. 

IS No. Title

3 GRADES 

This standard covers two grades of refined tin 
ingot, namely Sn 99 S and Sn 96 S- 

4 SUPPLY OF MATERIAL 

4.1 General requirements relating to the supply 
of tin ingot shall conform to IS 1387 : 1967. 

4.2 The tin may also be supplied in the form 
of bars/rods or plates, if agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer. 

5 MANUFACTURE 

Tin ingots shall be produced from secondary 
sources. 

6 CHEMICAL COMPOSITION 

6.1 The chemical composition of refined secon- 
dary tin ingots covered in this standard shall 
conform to the requirements given in Table 1. 

6.2 The chemical composition shall be deter- 
mined either by the methods specified in 
IS 1940 : 1969 or any other established instru- 
mental/chemical method. In case of dispute, the 
procedure specified in IS 1940: 1969 shall be 
the referred method.

analysis may be required and limits established for 
elements not specified. 



7 FREEDOM FROM DEFECTS 

Tin ingots shall be free from inclusions and 
other harmful defects. 

8 SAMPLING 

8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer, one ingot 
shall be selected from each consignment of 
1 000 kg or part thereof representing one grade 
of tin produced under uniform conditioas of 
manufacture and offered for inspection at one 
time. 

8.2 The method of preparing samples for 
chemical analysis from the ingots selected 
under 8.1 shall be in accordance with IS 1817 : 
1961. 



IS 4288 : 1992 



9 RETEST 

If the sample prepared under 8.2 and tested for 
chemical compt>sition fails to me^t tfefequire*- 
ments specified undier 6.1, two mor^ tests shall 
be conducted on the same sample ih ordtt to 
confirm that the analysis has been dbnfe pro* 
perly. If both the test results satisfy the 
relevant requirements the lot shall be accepted. 
Should either of the retest samples fail, the lot 
represented shall be deemed as not complying 
with this standard. 

10 INSPECTION 

10.1 AH inspection and testing of tin ingots 
covered in this standard shall be carried out by 
the manufacturer unless otherwise agreed to 
betWie^eft the mMufacturer and the purchaser. 
The ihspection requirements shall be stated in 
the enquiry and Order. 

10.2 The purchaser shall notify the supplier 
while placing the order if it is his intentioti to 
inspect the tin ingots at the supplier*s end* 
The supplier shall offer the purchaser all the 
necessary facilities for testing of the tin ingots 



in accordance with this standard. For this 
purpose the purchaser or his representative may, 
by prior arrangement, attend to inspect the tin, 
ingots to stiect and identify the test samples 
and to witness the testing. 

11 MARKING 

lt«l Each iiigot shall be legibly marked with 
the following: 

a) Cast/lot number, 

b) Grade of the tin, and 

c) Indication af th« source of msiaufacture. 

11.2 Standard Marking 

Each ingot may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 

12 TEST CERTIFICATE 

The supplier shall provide test certificate for 
each consignment giving information like cast/ 
lot number, corresponding chemical com- 
position, etc. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 2986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark 
on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been 
produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system 
of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and 
operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by 
BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under 
which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to 
promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced 
in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, 
in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type 
or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director 
( Publications ), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if 
any, are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in 
possession of the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard maybe 
sent to BIS giving the following reference:
